project_type: Python library + CLI (sars-convert / import package `sars`, src/ layout) that reconstructs Mwanza SARS Form-Two mock result PDFs as pure HTML+CSS and prints them to PDF via WeasyPrint. Two paths: `convert` (redraw one specific PDF) and `template` (data -> per-report recovered layout spec -> fixed-layout HTML -> PDF).
build_system: setuptools (PEP 517); dependency + venv management via uv (uv.lock, .python-version present). Editable install: `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`.
test_framework: pytest. tests/test_sars.py (unit + conversion fidelity), tests/test_fidelity_gate.py (the acceptance gate, marked `slow`). Run non-slow: `pytest -q -m "not slow"`; run the gate: `pytest -q -m slow`.
build_command: uv pip install -e ".[dev]"  (no compilation; pure Python).
test_command: pytest -q -m "not slow"  for fast tests; pytest -q -m slow  runs the full per-page pixel fidelity gate.
verification_instructions: Full regen + gate (from docs/FIDELITY_NOTES.md §8 / FIDELITY_SPEC.md §9): activate .venv, then `python tools/build_fonts.py` (REQUIRED, derives+installs reference faces from sars.zip); `python -m sars.cli data`; `python tools/build_layout_specs.py`; `python -m sars.cli template`; `python tools/compare.py`; `python tools/fidelity_gate.py --json output/fidelity/current.json`; compare worst-page-visible and per-report numbers against output/fidelity/baseline-verify.json (the captured baseline). The GUARDRAIL: no report's visible-pixel-match % may drop versus baseline in any change. Also run `python tools/slot_audit.py` to confirm no printed value is dropped, and `python tools/fidelity_report.py output/fidelity/current.json --baseline output/fidelity/baseline-verify.json` for a per-report delta table.
snapshot_or_generated_files: GENERATED, NOT COMMITTED (gitignored, rebuilt on demand): data/sars/** (from `sars unpack`), assets/fonts/** (from `tools/build_fonts.py`; redistributing Monotype Arial is deliberately excluded from git). COMMITTED build products under output/ (data/, html/, pdf/, template_html/, template_pdf/, compare/, ir/, fidelity/) regenerated by `sars data`, `sars all`, `sars template`, `tools/compare.py`, `tools/fidelity_gate.py`. Layout specs src/sars/templates/layouts/<name>.json.gz ARE committed and are rebuilt by `tools/build_layout_specs.py`. Baseline fidelity JSON captured at output/fidelity/baseline-verify.json.
setup_instructions: uv venv --python 3.11 .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -e ".[dev]" && python -m sars.cli unpack && python tools/build_fonts.py. Pango/Cairo/HarfBuzz present on the host. PyPI reachable (network allows package installs). WeasyPrint 70.0, PyMuPDF 1.28.2 installed.
environment_constraints: Network reaches PyPI (installs work). No Chromium binary present, so the engine bake-off falls back to WeasyPrint everywhere (assets/engine_choice.json already picks WeasyPrint for all 19). No Docker used. Fonts are NOT committed and MUST be rebuilt with tools/build_fonts.py before any render or gate; without them every report renders in Noto Sans and the gate collapses to 38-90%. The .venv and data/sars are freshly created in this session.
contribution_requirements: docs/FIDELITY_SPEC.md is the authoritative acceptance contract: the ONLY acceptance criterion is per-page visible-pixel identity from tools/fidelity_gate.py; text-similarity / page-size / page-count are diagnostics only. Anti-cheating rules (SPEC §5): do NOT loosen the gate threshold, sample fewer pages, shrink the raster, widen tolerance, or edit reference PDFs. PROJECT LEARNING (cross-cutting, mandatory): each report type is reproduced as its OWN fully self-contained HTML+CSS artefact (own spec, own inline style, own geometry); do NOT force a shared/global stylesheet or merge distinct reports' structures. Generalize the DATA model and the row-looping mechanism, but keep each report's visual template independent and faithful. Reference PDFs are read-only.
key_patterns: The `template` path is a mechanism, not per-report code: tools/build_layout_specs.py recovers each report's chrome + data bands into src/sars/templates/layouts/<name>.json.gz (page box, paint sequence of rectangles, chrome glyphs at exact origins, per-band column boxes/row pitch/fills/fonts/sizes/alignment/baseline + recovered column->data-field bindings). sars.layout_spec.render_html walks a spec and asks a ValueProvider for each (page, band, kind, row). sars.binding.row_groups(data) turns a schema instance into ordered named row groups ('rows','totals','students0','students1',...,'section0',...); binding_provider maps spec bands to those groups via the recovered `group`/`group_index`/`bindings`/`column_bindings`. Competency background colour is DERIVED at render time (sars.competency), never stored. Font metrics/advances/baseline offsets come from sars.fonts (built from the reference PDFs).

the_bug: output/compare/MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS.jpg: the second table (TOP TEN BEST FEMALE STUDENTS OVERALL COUNCILWISE) renders with only its caption and an empty body (no header row, no data rows), a large red diff region. Root cause confirmed: the extractor merges the two logical PDF tables on a page (overall + female, separated by a caption) into ONE lattice Table sharing column edges; tools/build_layout_specs.py then recovers ONE data band per page bound to a single student group (groups students0, students2, students4, students6 across the 5 pages), so odd-indexed sections (the female/male continuation tables) and the second table on each page get NO band and are never fed data. binding.row_groups produces students0..students8 (9 sections x 10 students); slot_audit reports 0 disagreements ONLY because it audits the bands the spec defines, and the missing table has no band. The fix must make band recovery + binding handle multiple tables/sections per page and bind each logical section to its own group, generalising the row-looping over sections.
